pack.title: Group-chat jabs
pack.description: Roasts with an audience of twelve. Win the thread without losing the friend.

scenarios.setting: The group chat. You share good news; a friend quote-tweets it with a jab.

replies.line: I'm happy about this news. I'd like to enjoy sharing it.
replies.why: It names your wish for the exchange without competing for status.
replies.delivery: Keep it light if the banter is welcome; use a plain tone if it has become hurtful.

replies.why: It steps over the jab and re-centers your news in five words.
replies.delivery: Keep it light if the banter is welcome; use a plain tone if it has become hurtful.

replies.line: I'm excited about it; I'd love to celebrate with you all.
replies.why: It offers connection around your good news rather than responding with a comparison.
replies.delivery: Keep it light if the banter is welcome; use a plain tone if it has become hurtful.

replies.line: Somebody has to carry this chat's plot.
replies.why: It joins welcome banter without insulting another person's achievements.
replies.delivery: Keep it light if the banter is welcome; use a plain tone if it has become hurtful.

trap.line: At least I HAVE news. What have you done lately?
trap.why: It replaces a specific request with accusation, resentment, or an excuse, making your actual boundary less clear.

scenarios.goal: Share good news without competing for status.

followUp.jab: Can't you take a little banter?
followUp.line: I can enjoy a joke; I'd also like to enjoy sharing my news.
followUp.why: It communicates the kind of participation you want without counterattacking.
followUp.delivery: Keep it light if the banter is welcome; use a plain tone if it has become hurtful.

scenarios.setting: The group chat. An old embarrassing photo of you resurfaces.
scenarios.jab: throwback to when you looked like THIS 💀

replies.line: I'd rather that photo stayed private. Please remove it.
replies.why: It gives an explicit consent boundary without attacking the sender.
replies.delivery: State your preference plainly; avoid pretending to laugh if you want it removed.

replies.line: I know you meant it playfully; I don't want that photo in the chat, so please remove it.
replies.why: It acknowledges intent while making the removal request clear.
replies.delivery: State your preference plainly; avoid pretending to laugh if you want it removed.

replies.line: We don't talk about the bangs era.
replies.why: It offers a self-directed joke if you genuinely welcome sharing the photo.
replies.delivery: State your preference plainly; avoid pretending to laugh if you want it removed.

replies.line: Please remove that photo from the chat.
replies.why: It states the immediate boundary without adding a personal judgment.
replies.delivery: State your preference plainly; avoid pretending to laugh if you want it removed.

scenarios.goal: Choose whether an embarrassing photo stays shared.

followUp.jab: It's just an old photo, relax.
followUp.line: I don't want it shared here; please remove it.
followUp.why: It makes consent the issue rather than arguing about whether the photo is funny.
followUp.delivery: State your preference plainly; avoid pretending to laugh if you want it removed.

scenarios.setting: A friend posts a private story about you to the group chat.
scenarios.jab: Everyone needs to hear what you told me last night.
scenarios.goal: Stop a private story from becoming public entertainment.

replies.line: That was private. Please don't share it here.
replies.why: It names the privacy boundary and asks for a specific action.
replies.delivery: Be brief in the group; move any longer discussion to a private conversation.

replies.why: It asks for confidentiality without retelling the private information.
replies.delivery: Be brief in the group; move any longer discussion to a private conversation.

replies.line: I told you that privately; I'd like it to stay between us.
replies.why: It clarifies the original context without shaming your friend in the group.
replies.delivery: Be brief in the group; move any longer discussion to a private conversation.

replies.line: That story didn't sign up for the group tour.
replies.why: A light metaphor makes the privacy boundary visible without revealing more.
replies.delivery: Be brief in the group; move any longer discussion to a private conversation.

followUp.line: It's private to me; please delete it and don't share more.
followUp.why: It makes your consent the issue rather than debating how interesting the story is.
followUp.delivery: Be brief in the group; move any longer discussion to a private conversation.
